comparison: Both address behavioral validation (C36-C38) showing experimental conditions were harder than controls. OpenEval rated this as SUPPORTED, finding the statistical evidence adequate. Peer reviewers rated it UNCERTAIN, expressing persistent concerns that differential difficulty confounds interpretation of neural results and that the response methodology (button press only on last trial) prevents proper assessment of participant performance.

Both evaluate specificity claims (C43-C44, C53, C60-C62) showing left area PF is not engaged during non-physical reasoning. Both rated this SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasized convergent evidence from whole-brain and ROI analyses. Peer reviewers confirmed 'solid evidence' for differences across reasoning types and accepted the negative result for fluid cognition.

Both address correlation analysis (C54-C55, C95) testing whether left area PF reflects coherent cognitive process. OpenEval rated SUPPORTED, viewing correlation as evidence for unified function. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, noting correlation 'does not rule out the so-called same region different function interpretation' and that one cannot reverse infer common function from correlation alone.

Both evaluate spatial analysis of peak coordinates (C56-C58, C96) addressing adjacency interpretation. OpenEval rated SUPPORTED, finding y-coordinate comparison provides quantitative evidence for same anatomical location. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, questioning why analysis was restricted to y-coordinate only and suggesting Euclidean distance across all coordinates would be more rigorous.

Both address claim C94 about difficulty confound. OpenEval rated SUPPORTED, viewing fluid cognition as adequate control showing difficulty alone doesn't drive activation. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, arguing the response 'sidesteps the central point' that fundamental computations may drive area PF to varying degrees, and fluid cognition comparison only shows those tasks don't tap the same computations.

Both evaluate dissociation between mentalizing and technical reasoning networks (C46-C48, C63-C64, plus C7 in peer review). Both rated SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasized contrast analysis isolating mentalizing-specific activation. Peer reviewers accepted the finding that distinct networks can work together, with one reviewer acknowledging area PF's role across both mentalizing conditions.

Both address core finding of consistent left area PF activation across technical reasoning tasks (C39-C42, C59, plus C5-C6, C49-C52 in peer review). Both rated SUPPORTED. OpenEval highlighted conjunction analysis as particularly strong evidence. Peer reviewers affirmed 'solid evidence' and 'valuable insights,' with editor noting enhanced reliability from additional analyses.

OpenEval R6 addresses ROI analysis (C49-C53) providing convergent evidence for whole-brain findings. Peer R1 includes these claims (C49-C52) as part of broader evaluation of core findings. Both rated SUPPORTED. OpenEval emphasized literature-defined ROI ensuring independence. Peer reviewers accepted ROI validation as enhancing reliability.

Both address main conclusions about dedicated neural system for technical reasoning (C5-C8 in OpenEval, C8-C9 in peer review). Both rated SUPPORTED. OpenEval found claim of 'specific cognitive module' justified by convergent evidence. Peer reviewers accepted core finding as 'valuable contribution' to understanding area PF computations, though speculative cultural transmission aspect (C9) was not explicitly challenged.

OpenEval R11 addresses broader theoretical claims about cultural evolution (C9, C72-C74, C98, C101) rated UNCERTAIN due to lack of direct testing. Peer R7 includes C9 but rates overall conclusions SUPPORTED. Peer reviewers did not explicitly challenge the speculative cultural transmission claims, focusing instead on the neural findings.

Both address interpretation of technical reasoning network beyond left area PF (C65, C67 in both, plus C33, C27 in peer review). OpenEval rated UNCERTAIN, noting speculative interpretations beyond current data. Peer reviewers rated UNCERTAIN, raising fundamental concern that discussion is 'narrowly construed' and overly focused on left SMG, suggesting network characterization may be incomplete.

OpenEval found methodological details about recruitment, sample sizes, and ethical approval (C34-C35, C85-C86) to be SUPPORTED as straightforward descriptive claims. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these methodological details were not specifically discussed in peer reviews.

OpenEval rated claims about morphometry work and right area PF interpretation (C68-C70) as UNCERTAIN, noting they cite prior work not directly tested and involve speculative interpretation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically address these claims.

OpenEval rated background and motivation claims (C1-C4, C10-C14, C97) as SUPPORTED, viewing them as appropriate framing supported by citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not evaluate these introductory contextual claims.

OpenEval rated literature review claims about neural basis of tool use (C15-C27) as SUPPORTED, finding them well-supported by citations and providing essential context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically evaluate these literature summary claims.

OpenEval rated definitional claims about technical-reasoning hypothesis (C28-C33) as SUPPORTED, viewing them as clear conceptual framework. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically evaluate these theoretical definitions, though C33 appears in peer R8's broader network concerns.

OpenEval rated claims defining fluid cognition and its neural basis (C75-C80) as SUPPORTED, finding them appropriately establish rationale for control condition. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically evaluate these definitional claims about fluid cognition.

OpenEval rated claims defining mentalizing and its neural basis (C81-C84) as SUPPORTED, viewing them as appropriate theoretical foundation. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically evaluate these definitional claims about mentalizing.

OpenEval rated methodological descriptions of tasks and ROI methodology (C87-C93) as SUPPORTED, finding them clearly documented and essential for replication. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically evaluate these methodological descriptions.

OpenEval rated claims citing prior research and characterizing field state (C71, C99-C100) as SUPPORTED, viewing them as appropriate context. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; reviewers did not specifically evaluate these contextual claims about the field.
